highlights.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
highlights.summary: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed on Tuesday that it's investigating a "cybersecurity incident." The bureau, which is part of the Treasury Department, said it's looking into an "incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." It hasn't…
body: FinCEN’s alert comes in the wake of a reported breach of unclassified information at US spy agencies, including the CIA.

The news comes hours after The New York Times reported that the Central Intelligence Agency and Office of the Director of National Security discovered a breach of an open source intelligence system, exposing unclassified information. The Department of Defense, whose National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency was also reportedly impacted by the breach, declined to comment. The CIA and ODNI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s unclear if the FinCEN breach is related. Americans have been on high alert about security incidents after a series of seemingly unrelated outages earlier this month.

FinCEN’s role is to protect the financial system from illegal activity, including by combatting money laundering and terrorism financing. The bureau maintains financial transaction data and distributes it for law enforcement purposes. FinCEN also houses reports of suspicious activity that financial institutions file as part of the Bank Secrecy Act.

The bureau, which is part of the Treasury Department, said it's looking into an "incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.

highlights.title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users “DJ their art”
highlights.summary: “TangiMap” uses an AI agent to reprogram how buttons, knobs, and sliders are used, helping users do things like edit photos and perform music in a more dynamic, tactile way.
body: In 2017, Apple removed the home button from its iPhones. Users lost a convenient, tangible control — part of a larger shift to digital buttons, knobs, and sliders we also see in cars (like with radio presets and air conditioning) and kitchens (see smart fridges).

We can’t leave physical controls behind entirely, though. They tend to be more convenient and efficient — think of how you can use a physical gaming controller without looking at it — and, at times, more precise, like when you use a dial to get the volume just right. But tangible controls are typically preprogrammed to do a specific thing, minimizing their usefulness.

highlights.title: Rangers 'dug it out' despite naivety & complacency - McInnes
highlights.summary: Rangers manager Derek McInnes says his team's naivety and complacency made their task more difficult in their thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen, but hails their ability to get the job done.
body: The Ibrox outfit had to navigate a tense finale as they held off a defiant Aberdeen side, just three days after their dramatic late win at Motherwell, and are now just a point behind Celtic at the Scottish Premiership summit.
Rangers had roared into a 3-1 lead after a stunning 11-minute burst at the start of the second half overwhelmed the visitors, who led at the break through Brad Lyons' header.
However, the Dons pulled one back through vibrant youngster Findlay Marshall and both sides had opportunities to add to the scoreline in a gripping closing passage.
"We put ourselves in the mire there, we were so naive at times," McInnes told Sky Sports.

highlights.title: GTA 6's Most Heartbreaking Scene Is Exactly Why You Had To Do All Those Chores
highlights.summary: Jason repairs the steps leading up to his and Lucia’s home, fixes a railing, buys groceries, orders flowers, paints the walls of their bedroom, and more to prepare for Lucia’s arrival from prison.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 features as much shootin’, stealin’, and drug runnin’ as you’d expect from the latest entry in a series named after a felony. However, some players have been caught off-guard by just how much the early game is all about the more mundane parts of life. Namely, you gotta do a bunch of chores around the house. In many ways, GTA 6 is as much of an everyday life sim as it is a game about committing crimes.

Chapter 1 involves Jason and Lucia trying to get work from Mattia, the shady boyfriend of Kat, a mother-to-be whom Lucia befriended in prison. Part of that involves a standout sequence set to a Carly Rae Jepsen banger before Lucia gets lost in orgy central. (Vice City, y’all!) Bro, Mattia promises a job that could pay ten grand, bro. They just have to grab a bag from a locker and deliver it, bro.

Red flags abound, but Jason and Lucia go along for the ride, which quickly results in their arrest. Crooked cops show up, the couple gets into a shootout, and Jason gets grievously wounded while the couple struggle to keep hold over a bag containing who knows what.

highlights.title: Why tiny cars are taking off across Europe
highlights.summary: Once seen as a car for elderly, rural people, tiny cars are being embraced by a younger demographic.
body: Selena Buse, 16, reverses her Citroën Ami out of a parking space and heads off past the school playground. Heads turn. The Ami looks pretty remarkable. Futurist or like-a-toaster depending on your point of view. But it's changed her life.
"I got it because I really needed it to get to school. And I use it to visit friends on the weekends. It's indispensable in rural areas like where I live," she says.
In France, you can drive a car like this from the age of 14 with a road safety certificate and eight hours training. In Italy too.
In Germany and Spain it's 15, in the UK 16. Because they are classed as motorised quadri-cycles. Four-wheel mopeds in other words.

highlights.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
highlights.summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether…
body: Investors cheered Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday, but renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale thinks they’re celebrating a mistake. He sees a company that is largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher. Far from a champion of American industry, he says, Nvidia is “a detriment to U.S. global industrial might.”

As evidence, Sonnenfeld points to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S. export controls and to sinking shares of Anthropic, which he links to the realization that China’s seemingly miraculous open source AI models are, in a sense, copies of top U.S. labs’ work, even as Nvidia has insisted that smuggling is a “non-factor.”
Indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with just as much enthusiasm in Asia, The Washington Post reported. “The king is back!” read one headline from China’s state-affiliated Star Market Daily.

highlights.title: 'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt
highlights.summary: Manchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt, as displayed in their laborious Champions League draw against Napoli.
body: The quick passing patterns and edge-of-the-seat action that was evident for so long under former manager Pep Guardiola was supposed to be taken forward by incumbent Enzo Maresca.
It started flawlessly under the Italian with the side winning their first eight games, but that smooth operation is beginning to turn into a turgid and pedestrian showing.
Similar to Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham, moans and groans filled a rather flat Etihad Stadium as the home faithful watched their side labour to a 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli.
City's recent defensive issues also continued, now conceding in 10 successive games and letting in the first goal in seven of those matches.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang’s Return Shows Nvidia Is Too Big to Police
highlights.summary: Nvidia’s place at the center of the US economy may have outweighed concerns about its CEO’s ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, national security and foreign policy experts say.
body: Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO signals that the chipmaker may have grown too important to the stock market for the US government to hold it accountable for national security lapses, intelligence and export-control experts warn WIRED. The move also undercuts the warnings Washington routinely issues to American companies and foreign governments about Beijing’s pursuit of US technology, they say.

Nvidia’s board brought back Huang on Monday, 11 days after he resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs —one of them with Alice Huang, a woman US intelligence suspects has ties to China’s Ministry of State Security. The board said input from “senior levels of the United States government” left it confident that his return poses no national security risk.

highlights.summary: Famous Dutch-Belgian race driver Max Verstappen revealed that he’d spent the weekend of the Las Vegas Grand Prix locked in to GTA 6, saying he played over 40 hours of the game. Everyone’s got GTA 6 fever, including Max Verstappen.
body: Verstappen nonchalantly dropped this nugget of information during a live stream the following week, saying he would play the game in the mornings and evenings in between his duties on the track.
“I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas,” Verstappen explained. “I mean, I can’t go out anyways and walk around.”
The driver also revealed that he’s been so focused on GTA 6 and driving real-life race cars that he’s “completely forgotten” how to play Minecraft, despite having a scheduled stream for it.
“I’m so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can’t, I just can’t!” he joked.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Employees in First All-Hands Since His Return
highlights.summary: The Nvidia CEO opened up about his personal life, defended his reinstatement, and acknowledged that his intense management style had hurt his staff.
body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday that the company’s code of conduct allows room for a “second chance,” that succession planning is a “flawed’ process,” and that he would work to rein in his “insanely intense” management style, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED.

During his first all-hands since returning as CEO, Huang acknowledged that he violated the company’s policies and made some “very serious personal mistakes” that damaged his relationships with his wife and two children and prompted him to resign. But he said Nvidia’s board of directors made the appropriate decision for the company in welcoming him back. He added that the board made that call, not “the highest levels of our government.”

Huang spoke for about an hour, offering deeply personal thoughts about his therapy sessions and drawing applause at times from employees at Nvidia’s Silicon Valley headquarters as he spoke about the company’s success and future. He didn’t take any questions. While some Nvidia employees celebrated Huang’s return, others remained concerned about his behavior and the board’s decision to reinstate him.
points: The Nvidia CEO opened up about his personal life, defended his reinstatement, and acknowledged that his intense management style had hurt his staff.

The draw leaves City in sixth spot in the Champions League table but they are likely to drop out of the top eight by Wednesday evening and have now gone 10 games without a clean sheet. Maresca's men look vulnerable ahead of the trip to Arsenal on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

Haaland speaking to TNT Sports said: "We tried to push but we couldn't. It's not good enough. We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want. Football can be so difficult and easy. When you win games everything is easy and you know exactly what to do, when you don't win you start to question everything. The perfect thing would be to don't think, but it's difficult in these moments.
"We have so much quality. It's about getting that quality out of every single player. We have to regroup to stay positive and bring the energy on the pitch.

highlights.title: Black Friday Streaming Deals: Everything You Need to Know Before You Subscribe
highlights.summary: Pretty much every service (other than good ol' Netflix) has announced a Black Friday deal for 2026, offering a rare respite from the onslaught of price hikes.
body: Streaming prices have been going up for years now, with no sign they'll ever come back down. To make matters worse, streaming deals have become increasingly rare, and there's really only one time of year when services offer a discount.

These deals are by far the best way to try out a new service or lock down your favorites for their cheapest price of the year, but some services are being more generous than others. A few are even offering 12-month deals that cover you until the next round of Black Friday discounts.

Scroll on for a deeper breakdown of our top picks, but the TL;DR is that Disney+ and Hulu are offering the only bundle deal of the year, while Apple TV, Paramount+, and Crunchyroll are splurging with discounts on ad-free plans. Peacock decided to bring back its Black Friday deal after skipping the festivities in 2025, but Netflix is still completely MIA and likely always will be.

Disney+ and Hulu have brought back the exact same Black Friday deal they offered in 2025. The Basic bundle with ads is down to $4.99/month for a 12-month period. However, after another round of Disney+ price hikes, the deal technically offers better savings than last year.

highlights.title: ‘The food of emperors’: a Chinese restaurant turns boring turkeys into crispy showstoppers
highlights.summary: Chicago’s Sun Wah BBQ started a new Turkey Day tradition for immigrants and other neighbors: allowing them to bring in their fowl and roast it in the fragrant Hong Kong-style. Tell us: do you have a special new year food tradition?
body: Behind an Uptown Chicago facade of glass and green-glazed bricks, rows of mahogany-red ducks glisten.

This neighborhood is sometimes called “New Chinatown”, sometimes “Little Vietnam ”. And this tidy restaurant is Sun Wah BBQ, which Eric and Lynda Cheng opened in 1987. Today, it’s also an unlikely Thanksgiving destination.

Every November, customers bring their own turkeys to Sun Wah to be prepared in the style of a Hong Kong roast duck. This year, the Cheng family will roast close to 200 turkeys, thanks to a TikTok video that increased demand. But this annual tradition, turning pale workaday turkeys into gorgeously lacquered holiday centerpieces, began as an informal favor about two decades ago.

highlights.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
highlights.summary: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter.
body: The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover’s communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.

One of the rover’s two UHF radios was unresponsive when it powered up on October 30, triggering an automatic switch to the backup radio and placing the rover in safe mode. Ground teams at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California later discovered the backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output, NASA said in a statement last week.
“The team has stopped using both radios until they can evaluate potential causes of the issues and one or both are deemed safe to resume operating,” NASA said.

highlights.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
highlights.summary: Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen.
body: The music streaming platform estimates that it will delete 29 million songs as a result of the AI ban.

The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 percent AI-generated. In a post on X, Andersen says Tidal needed to take a more “drastic” measure, as AI music made up 43 percent of the tracks distributed to the platform in the last 90 days. “We believe this will resonate with both artists and listeners alike, as 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays at all,” Andersen adds.

Bandcamp similarly banned AI music earlier this year, while other music streaming platforms attempt to address a flood of AI songs by applying new labels or removing them from user algorithms. Spotify recently announced that it removed 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from recommendations over the past year, and also launched new “AI persona” badges for artists that use an AI identity. YouTube has rolled out AI music labels as well, while Apple Music is planning to launch AI labels this year. Meanwhile, Deezer is giving users the option to filter out AI music.

highlights.title: Some GTA 6 Fans Love Chapter 1 for Its Slower Pace and Are Spending Dozens of Hours Roleplaying in It
highlights.summary: GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.
body: Warning: This article features light spoilers for the early hours of GTA 6.

Instead of throwing you headfirst into crazy heists or explosive set pieces, the first chapter of GTA 6 is largely spent bumbling around Rockstar's version of the Florida Keys. You can go fishing, scuba diving, and even fix up your house before Lucia's release from prison. It's an exceptionally low-key and chill opening to a game filled with all kinds of crazy action, which is why it's also rubbed some people the wrong way. They don't want to do chores or kick it on the beach; they want to cause some mayhem.

However, for others, this has become an unexpected hook for GTA 6 that actually delayed their interest in getting to the meat of Rockstar's open-world epic. Various fans of the game have said they spent anywhere from 10 to as many as 40+ hours in just Chapter 1 alone. Keep in mind, this is a sliver of the overall experience, and much of the game's most interesting activities don't get added until subsequent chapters. However, some players just enjoyed living inside of this part of the game before things go horribly wrong and they're forced to start ramping up the violence and crime.

body: Over the last few years, lymphatic drainage has gone from an IYKYK technique to an all-out wellness obsession. Oft described as the “Cinderella of medicine,” the lymphatic system is responsible for collecting excess fluid from tissues, transporting immune cells, and carrying certain waste products away from cells. This system, however, doesn’t work on its own to get the lymph flowing. Lymphatic drainage is a more manual practice; you can try your hand at deep breathing or dry brushing, but few things offer offer as excellent lifting benefits as the best gua sha tools.

“The literal gua sha Mandarin translation is ‘to scrape sand,’” explains Lin Chen, cofounder of Pink Moon. “Gua sha tools have been used as a unique approach for holistic healing in China for 4,000 years. It has been traditionally used over the body to help aid in the movement of qi (which is energy flow), increase circulation, and release tension.” That said, Chen continues saying that research shows that the practice was first used in the Paleolithic Ages, dating back to the Ming dynasty in China.

highlights.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
highlights.summary: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.
body: Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US.
In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.
Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.
Huawei said, external the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis", adding that it would "take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests".

highlights.title: Jensen Huang deepfakes are the hot new AI slop
highlights.summary: Jensen Huang is partying it up in Ibiza. In a video with nearly 6 million views on Instagram, the former CEO of Nvidia is dancing in a crowded club, champagne glass in hand, still wearing his signature black leather jacket.
body: Influencers are chasing viral success with the saga — and tech stack — of Nvidia’s CEO.

Unlike deepfake pornography or election disinformation, these AI videos aren’t necessarily intended to harm or mislead people. They’re memes making fun of Huang’s cheating scandal and its global implications, created with AI technology that in many cases relies heavily on Nvidia’s tech stack: video diffusion models running on the Nvidia GPUs that power much of the modern generative AI industry. “It’s ironic that without Nvidia generating millions of these AI memes... would not be possible,” reads one of the top comments on the Ibiza deepfake. “In some sense, Jensen is making Nvidia richer by his own scandal.” The comment was punctuated by multiple cry-laughing emoji.

highlights.title: McIlroy misses out on PGA Tour player of the year shortlist - who is in?
highlights.summary: Rory McIlroy has missed out on being shortlisted for the PGA Tour's Player of the Year award, despite successfully defending his title at The Masters.
body: McIlroy became the first player since Tiger Woods to win at Augusta National in successive years, following his one-shot victory over Scottie Scheffler, with the world No 2 adding three further top-four finishes on the PGA Tour during the season.

The six-time major champion is a three-time winner of the Jack Nicklaus Award but a noticeable absentee on the five-man shortlist for the 2026 season, announced Tuesday after being finalised by the PGA Tour Player Directors and the Player Advisory Council (PAC).

Wyndham Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick, Chris Gotterup, Scottie Scheffler and Cameron Young were the five players nominated, with the Player of the Year award then decided by votes from PGA Tour members who have played at least 15 tournaments over the season.

Scheffler won three times on the PGA Tour this season, including The American Express and two of the three FedExCup Playoffs, with the world No 1 looking to break another Woods record by winning the award for a fifth consecutive year.

highlights.title: How to flip your car in GTA 6
highlights.summary: Flipping your car in Grand Theft Auto 6 works a bit differently than it did in previous games. In Rockstar's bid for realism, the team made it so you can't flip your car while you're still in it. Instead, whichever character you're controlling will have to get out of the car and turn it over.
body: If you manage to turn over your sedan, ATV, boat, or cement truck, and you do it without getting wasted ( GTA 6 's term for "destroying it completely and dying"), you might think you'll have to get Scooter Bros to deliver the vehicle for you. Well, you don't. Keep that hard-stolen cash in your BuckMe account and fix it yourself.
And you're good to go on your merry way. That said, there are a few caveats to bear in mind if you're trying to flip your car.

Try to push the car from the middle. If you're at either end of it, we noticed the prompt tends not to appear. Also, if there's an obstacle on the other side of the car, like a thick hedge or a wall, you won't be able to flip it. The same is true for when your car is just stuck on something, like a guardrail. The game won't let you flip it off the offending object, as it has to be completely upended for the "shove" prompt to appear.
points: Flipping your car in Grand Theft Auto 6 works a bit differently than it did in previous games.
In Rockstar's bid for realism, the team made it so you can't flip your car while you're still in it.
Instead, whichever character you're controlling will have to get out of the car and turn it over.

highlights.title: Clash Royale recruits creator of AI cheating tool to help catch cheaters
highlights.summary: Clash Royale developer Supercell has recruited the creator of an advanced AI cheating tool to help crack down on cheating in the game.
body: AI cheating has become a growing controversy in Clash Royale, with increasingly sophisticated bots reportedly capable of outperforming skilled human players. Players highlighted claims that an AI-controlled account named ‘Clasher’ had reached the top of the game’s global leaderboard.

The situation prompted calls for Supercell to intervene, with the developer addressing the controversy on November 20. In a statement posted on X, Clash Royale warned that using AI or other tools to cheat was a “royal crime,” declaring that offending players would be banished from the Arena.
On November 21, the official Clash Royale X account announced that it had caught the creator of an AI cheating tool and recruited them to help develop new anti-cheat technology.

“The creator of the AI cheating tool has been caught,” Supercell announced in a statement framed as a royal decree from the King. “He’s agreed, entirely of his own free will, to join forces with the Clash Royale team.
